criteria.RV01: Actual FY22–25 movements and period screens qualify. All 2026 cohort terms excluded.
criteria.RV02: Opening-share ratios bound programme size only. Treasury transfer differs from new issuance.
criteria.RV03: Deeply discounted repeat issuance is meaningful. Older economic exposure and protections are insufficiently established.
criteria.RV04: Historical authorization is evidence of process. Exact profitability attribution and recipient-level retention are absent.
criteria.RV05: Long-run EPS and FCF context is partly favorable. The FY2025 FCF/share decline limits corroboration and is not itself an ESOP loss.
criteria.RV06: Accept N/R at 5/10. Neither proposed band is established. Confidence assesses sufficiency, not the direction of net transfer.

blockers.finding: N/R. The pattern supports a meaningful recurrent discount risk, while the eligible historic terms and exposure coverage do not demonstrate programme-wide control or sufficiently establish realized material detriment. The absence of quantified benefits is not the decision predicate.

criteria.RV01: June share, cohort terms, raw quote and gross cash receipts were checked against the eligible freeze.
criteria.RV02: Share denominators reconcile. Actual quote remains a sensitivity and gross cash is not net proceeds.
criteria.RV03: Economics challenge defeats the 1/1 hypothesis. The protections do not demonstrate control of recurrent discount economics.
criteria.RV04: Contractual protections are substantive. The 70/30 formula with zero TSR, unexplained 5,332-share gap and absence of a cash trigger temper control.
criteria.RV05: Neither group outcome nor absence of proven harm supports a positive band. Cash deterioration and FTEL scope limit inference.
criteria.RV06: Accept N/R at 6/10. Adverse exposure is evidenced in scenarios but actual programme-wide shareholder detriment remains unestablished.

blockers.finding: N/R. The terms and filings establish actual design controls, and the documented award size bounds ownership dilution for June. Neither controls the economic transfer across recurring awards. Deep discount, a sizable transfer range, no demonstrated cash-oriented trade-off and weak FY2025 cash corroboration defeat the positive hypothesis. The completion quote and historic screens do not establish net shareholder detriment. Plausible benefits remain uncredited and unknown.
